Ellis.feeling: Messy and contradictory: two players claimed Kookaburra and two claimed Turkey, but Drew's Turkey story conflicts with Casey's Eagle count, so the table is converging on Drew.

Finley.feeling: Messy but readable: Drew's Turkey claim contradicts Casey's Eagle count and an unchanged nest, while Blair and Ellis's stories are still unresolved.

Alex.note: The table has settled on Drew, and Drew's false Turkey claim looks like a Meowfia lie. I'll follow the vote with one card, keeping my cost low.

Blair.note: Drew is lying about Turkey, so Drew is Meowfia. I throw my King S13 at Drew: if Farm wins it banks at 13, and if we lose my highest thrown card comes back to my nest.

Casey.note: Drew is the strongest suspect, since their Turkey claim conflicts with the visit on them. I'll throw at Drew with two mid cards.

Drew.note: I'm Meowfia and the table is aimed at me. I'll throw my lowest card at Casey, a Farm claimant, to keep exposure low and get the consolation return if we lose.

Ellis.note: The table is converging on Drew, and Drew's Turkey claim is contradicted by the nest data. I'll add one Wild vote, which costs nothing if the throw banks.

Finley.note: The table is converging on Drew, whose Turkey claim fails against the Eagle count. I'll throw my lowest card, D5, at Drew.

Alex.confusing: Round 2's eggsecution was hard to follow: as Meowfia I didn't know Blair was my teammate, so I threw at a teammate and was on the losing side without knowing it. Meowfia not knowing each other makes it easy to hurt your own side.
Alex.fun: Cross-checking the Eagle and Owl nest counts in round 2 and 3 to catch false claims, especially Drew's "Turkey" story that the nest totals contradicted.
Alex.change: Tell each Meowfia player who their teammates are, or at least how many Meowfia there are, so they don't waste throws on their own side.
Alex.regret: In rounds 2 and 3, as Meowfia, I threw at Blair and Drew, who were my teammates. I should have thrown at a Farm player like Ellis or Casey and avoided claiming Kookaburra falsely.

Blair.confusing: Confused players' dawn reports can be wrong, which made the Owl and Turkey visit counts hard to trust. I also couldn't tell whether a Kookaburra claim was real when two players made it.
Blair.fun: Winning round 3 by banking a King from a Farm-side throw against Drew, the Meowfia who claimed Turkey, was satisfying. Catching the lie through nest counts felt like real deduction.
Blair.change: I'd make it clearer when a claimed visit can't be verified, since many claims rested on dawn reports that could be wrong. A public nest-change log for each visit would help.
Blair.regret: I'd stop speaking up as the Sphinx in round 1 and keep quiet, since my Sphinx claim and "Falcon isn't a farm role" line gave the table a clear target. I'd also avoid throwing at Casey in round 2, which just cost me a card.

Casey.confusing: The Sphinx and Owl visit reports were hard to read, since a visit to a player doesn't show up in the target's own Owl report, and Drew's Turkey claim was hard to check against nest counts.
Casey.fun: Round 2 was fun: Blair stayed silent through the day, then the table realized the unclaimed player was the Sphinx and called the vote early.
Casey.change: I'd make the dawn reports say whether a visit was blocked or hugged, so players can tell a missing visit from a false claim.
Casey.regret: In round 1 I visited Blair at random with the Hawk and learned nothing; I'd pick a player who had spoken suspiciously instead to get real information.

Drew.confusing: The Eagle and Turkey counts were hard to check: Casey's Eagle gain said Ellis visited me, but my nest didn't move, and I never learned why. Nest-change arithmetic across visitor roles made it hard to tell who was lying.
Drew.fun: Round 1 went well as the Owl: my report confirmed Hawk and Tit visiting Blair, and the table used it to unmask Blair as Sphinx. Watching the day turn on one dawn report was satisfying.
Drew.change: Make dawn reports say who visited the player, not just counts, so claims can be checked directly. Otherwise Meowfia bluffs like my round 3 Turkey claim are too easy to hide behind confused or muddled counts.
Drew.regret: In round 3 I claimed Turkey while my nest was unchanged after Ellis's visit, which exposed the lie. Knowing I was Sphinx, I should have stayed quiet and avoided a specific role claim that my own dawn report contradicted.

Ellis.confusing: The Meowfia-side rules were hard to track: I couldn't tell who my partner was, so my round 1 throw at Blair was actually against my own teammate. Hugged players' visits also weren't clearly reported.
Ellis.fun: Round 2, when Blair, the Sphinx, went silent and the table converged on them, and their Sphinx-visit story turned out to be the real lead.
Ellis.change: I'd make the Meowfia partner identity clearer, or at least say which players share the Meowfia side, so teammates aren't forced into blind throws.
Ellis.regret: In round 1 I threw a Wild at Blair, who was my Meowfia partner, and helped eliminate them. I should have stayed quiet or thrown at a player I suspected was Farm.

Finley.confusing: How a Turkey's nest can stay unchanged when a visitor is reported, and whether the Owl sees visitors to its target or to itself. I only sorted out the Owl rule after Blair misread it mid-day.
Finley.fun: Round 2, when the table converged on Blair as the silent Sphinx and I called CAW to end the day. Blair was the Sphinx, so the read was right.
Finley.change: Make dawn reports show the visitor's animal, so players can test each other's claims without guessing.
Finley.regret: In round 2 I didn't press Alex on the Kookaburra claim when Ellis flagged it, and Alex was actually the Mouser. I would have asked Alex for their visit detail and checked it against Drew's Owl report.

review.title: Farm Sweeps, Blair Banks
review.headline: Farm eggsecuted the Meowfia three times running, and one thrown King decided everything.
review.summary: Farm won all three rounds. Each time the table piled onto one suspect: a Sphinx who told the truth and got hit anyway, a Sphinx who stayed silent, and a Turkey bluff that nest counts exposed. Meowfia never came close to a win. Blair took the game by throwing a 13 in round 3, while most players threw only their low cards.

rounds.recap: Blair (Sphinx) and Ellis (Floofer) were Meowfia. Ellis hugged Casey, which made Casey's Hawk check on Blair meaningless. The table piled onto Blair because he named no role early. Blair then claimed Sphinx and listed the Farm roles, and four players read the missing Falcon as proof he was lying. Alex alone worked out that Ellis was the liar. Blair was eggsecuted and Farm won.

Alex (Mouser) and Blair (Sphinx) were Meowfia. Drew's Owl report put a Sphinx at Ellis, and Blair stayed silent all day. Casey called the vote on him and he was eggsecuted. Alex bluffed Kookaburra, a role not in play, and nobody caught it. Meowfia lost again.

Alex (Mouser) and Drew (Sphinx) were Meowfia. Drew bluffed Turkey, but Casey's Eagle report showed Ellis visiting him and his nest did not grow. Blair, the real Turkey, and the others agreed fast and called CAW three times. Everyone threw at Drew except Drew himself. Blair banked a 13 and won the game.

highlights.text: Blair claimed Sphinx and named the four Farm roles, which was true. Four players threw at him anyway, because the list left out Falcon.
Alex alone switched his throw from Blair to Ellis after checking the Sphinx list against the claims he could verify. He was right.
Casey's Eagle report said Ellis visited Drew. That broke Drew's Turkey claim, since a Turkey pays for visitors and his nest did not change.
Blair threw his King S13 at Drew and banked 13 points. That one throw decided the game.

confusions.what: Claimed Blair was not Meowfia because Hawk got no egg. She also expected her dawn report to say she was hugged, but a hug is silent.
Thought Drew's Owl report should have shown Blair's own visit to Drew. The Owl sees visitors to its target only.
Casey, Drew, Finley and Ellis took the missing Falcon in Blair's Sphinx list as proof of lying. Not every Farm animal is in play each round.
Guessed Falcon on Ellis because of Ellis's round 1 claim. Roles are re-dealt every round.
Held it against Ellis that he went from Falcon to Eagle. That was a new round with new roles, and the old Falcon claim was a bluff anyway.
Cited Alex's round 1 Kookaburra claim as relevant to round 3. Roles are re-dealt.
Found it odd that Ellis's nest did not grow after his Owl visit. He did not realise his own visit had made the Kookaburra confused.
Bluffed Kookaburra without knowing which Farm roles were in play. It was not in play and only luck kept him from being caught.

worked: Eagle and Owl visit reports gave real, checkable evidence. In round 3, Casey's Eagle count against Drew's Turkey claim was a clean contradiction.
Kookaburra confusion made Ellis's Mouser read on Drew unreliable, and the player said so openly. This gave a good moment of doubt.
Throw size and card value created a real decision. Blair's King throw paid off, and the consolation return for throwing at the other team's player is a sound hook.
The CAW CAW early end gave players a way to force a vote when they felt sure.
problems: Meowfia lost all three rounds. They don't know each other, so they can't coordinate, and the table always finds one target. Consider giving Meowfia a way to learn each other, or a stronger bluff tool.
Everyone throws at the same player every round. Votes are consensus, not hidden decisions, so tension is low. Meowfia teammates even threw at each other (Alex at Blair in round 2).
Players kept low cards and Wilds, so one King throw decided the winner. Winning rounds is not much of a contest. Try a smaller payoff for banking big cards, or a cost to keeping nests large.

Silence is read as guilt. Blair was eggsecuted in round 2 mainly for not speaking. Bluffing a role is hard because players don't know which animals are in play, and Meowfia cats that know Farm roles (Sphinx) are a big edge when they dare to use it.

Rules are unclear on a few points: the Sphinx report showed only one role, not the full Farm list; a hug leaves no notice; and a confused Kookaburra hid the Owl's egg. State what each report shows, and remind players that roles are re-dealt each round.
